title: Greenfield Python CLI web scraper with file-based cache
description: Build a Python CLI tool from scratch that fetches a URL, extracts hyperlinks, and caches results to disk.

task_spec.prompt: Create a Python CLI tool from scratch. Structure: src/scraper.py with a main() entry point and an extract_links(html: str) -> list[str] function, tests/test_scraper.py with at least 3 tests, and pyproject.toml with requires-python>=3.11 and pytest as a dev dependency. Requirements: (1) Accept --url <URL> via argparse. (2) Fetch with urllib.request.urlopen (stdlib only, no requests/httpx). (3) extract_links() returns unique hrefs found in <a href="..."> tags using a simple regex. (4) File-based cache: store raw HTML at .cache/<hostname>.html; read from cache on repeat calls for same hostname instead of fetching. (5) Print each unique href on its own line to stdout. Tests must mock urllib.request.urlopen and verify: (a) extract_links returns expected list, (b) cache file is written on first call, (c) second call reads from cache without calling urlopen again. Run uv run pytest tests/ -v to confirm all tests pass.
success_criteria: extract_links() correctly parses hrefs from HTML
Cache read/write logic works as specified
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
